# Behavioral Specification: TL-UL Adapter for SRAM-like Devices

## 1. Purpose

The module bridges a TileLink-UL (TL-UL) bus to a simple synchronous SRAM-like memory interface. It accepts TL-UL read and write requests, translates them into SRAM accesses, and returns the corresponding TL-UL responses.

The adapter is intended for memories that do not themselves implement TL-UL. It must handle only single-transaction requests; burst transactions are not supported. Each accepted TL-UL request must result in at most one SRAM access.

## 2. Configuration

The adapter must be configurable with the following options:

- **SRAM address width**: selects the width of the address presented to the SRAM.
- **SRAM data width**: selects the width of the SRAM data word. The SRAM data width must be a multiple of the TL-UL data width and must be byte-granular.
- **Maximum outstanding transactions**: limits the number of accepted TL-UL requests that may be waiting for completion at one time. The default is one outstanding transaction.
- **Byte access enable**: controls whether partial-word writes are permitted.
- **Write-enable / read-enable policy**: the adapter may be configured to reject all writes, to reject all reads, or to allow both. It must not be configured to reject both reads and writes.
- **Command integrity checking**: enables checking of integrity information carried with incoming TL-UL commands.
- **Response integrity generation**: enables generation of integrity information for TL-UL responses.
- **Data integrity generation**: enables generation of integrity information for the data portion of TL-UL responses.
- **Data integrity pass-through**: enables passing pre-existing data integrity information through the adapter between the TL-UL side and the SRAM side.

Data integrity generation and data integrity pass-through are mutually exclusive. They may both be disabled. The SRAM data path must be widened when data integrity pass-through is enabled, because the memory is assumed to store the integrity bits alongside the data.

## 3. Transaction Acceptance and Ordering

The adapter must accept a TL-UL request only when it has enough internal tracking capacity to complete the transaction without loss. If accepting another request would exceed the configured maximum number of outstanding transactions, the adapter must not accept a new request.

For a normal request that will be sent to the SRAM, the adapter must also require the SRAM-side grant before accepting the request. The adapter may present the SRAM request before grant is asserted, but it must not consider the SRAM access accepted until grant is asserted.

Requests that are detected as errors must be accepted even if the SRAM-side grant has not been asserted, because such requests must not be sent to the SRAM.

The adapter must preserve the ordering of accepted requests. Responses must be returned in the same order as the corresponding requests were accepted. A response must not be presented to the TL-UL host until the previous response has been accepted by the host.

Each response must carry the same source identifier and the same size value as the corresponding request. The response opcode must indicate whether the transaction was a read or a write.

## 4. Request Error Handling

The adapter must check each incoming TL-UL request for the following error conditions:

- The request violates the TL-UL protocol, for example by using an undefined opcode, an invalid size, an invalid mask, or a misaligned address.
- A partial-word write is attempted while byte access is disabled. In this case, only write operations that cover the full TL-UL data word and use the full byte mask are allowed.
- A write is attempted while writes are disabled by configuration.
- A read is attempted while reads are disabled by configuration.
- An instruction-fetch-type request is attempted while the instruction fetch enable input indicates that instruction fetches are not enabled.
- Command integrity checking is enabled and the incoming command fails the integrity check.

If any of these error conditions applies, the adapter must:

1. Not issue the request to the SRAM.
2. Accept the request on the TL-UL side.
3. Return an error response.

The error response must use the response opcode appropriate to the request type: an error for a write must be returned as a write acknowledgement with the error flag asserted; an error for a read must be returned as a read data response with the error flag asserted. In both cases, the response error flag must be asserted.

A command integrity failure must also cause the dedicated sticky integrity error output to be asserted. Once asserted, this output must remain asserted until reset. The sticky status must not by itself cause later commands to be rejected; it is an indication that an integrity failure has occurred.

## 5. SRAM Access Behavior

For each non-erroring request, the adapter must generate a single SRAM access.

The SRAM request must carry:

- A request type identifying whether the transaction is an instruction fetch or a data access.
- A write-enable indication, asserted for TL-UL write commands and deasserted for TL-UL read commands.
- An SRAM address.
- For writes, the write data and a byte-level write mask.
- For reads, the request is presented with write-enable deasserted.

The adapter must hold the SRAM request asserted until the SRAM side grants the access. The request is delivered only when request and grant are asserted together.

The adapter must not issue a request to the SRAM for any request that has been determined to be an error.

Successful write requests are complete on the SRAM side once granted. The adapter must not wait for any SRAM write-acknowledge or read-data-valid signal before generating the TL-UL write response. After the write request is granted, the adapter must eventually return a write acknowledgement response when all earlier responses have been delivered.

Successful read requests must wait until the SRAM returns read data. When the read data is returned, the adapter must form the TL-UL read response from that data.

## 6. Read Data and Memory Errors

The SRAM read status may distinguish between correctable and uncorrectable memory errors. The adapter must use only the uncorrectable error indication to assert the TL-UL response error flag. A correctable error indication must not by itself cause the response error flag to be asserted.

When an uncorrectable error is reported with read data, the adapter must still return the read data along with the asserted error flag.

The adapter must return read data only for the byte lanes that were requested. For normal operation, inactive byte lanes in the response data must be returned as zeros.

## 7. Wide SRAM Word Support

The SRAM data width may be wider than the TL-UL data width. In this case, a TL-UL address can select a byte within a TL-UL word, and the TL-UL word can be embedded within a wider SRAM word.

The adapter must map the TL-UL address to the appropriate SRAM word address. The low-order address bits that select the byte or TL-UL sub-word must not be passed as part of the SRAM word address; instead, they must be used to determine which byte lanes and which portion of the SRAM word are involved.

For writes:

- The write data must be placed in the correct position within the SRAM word.
- The byte-enable mask must be placed at the correct position.
- Byte lanes not selected by the TL-UL mask must be masked off in the SRAM write mask.

For reads:

- The adapter must select the correct TL-UL word slice from the wide SRAM word.
- Only the requested byte lanes within that slice must be forwarded to the TL-UL response data.
- All other response data bytes must be zero.

The SRAM address presented by the adapter must be derived from the low-order SRAM word-address bits of the TL-UL address. The adapter intentionally has no base-address register and does not check whether the address falls within a particular memory region. If the surrounding system maps a region larger than the SRAM, addresses that exceed the SRAM address range may alias to lower SRAM addresses.

## 8. Data Integrity Behavior

### 8.1 Command Integrity

When command integrity checking is enabled, the adapter must validate the integrity information carried with each incoming request. A failed check must be treated as a request error and must also assert the sticky integrity error output. The request must not be forwarded to the SRAM.

When command integrity checking is disabled, incoming command integrity information must be ignored for error-checking purposes.

### 8.2 Response Integrity Generation

When response integrity generation is enabled, the adapter must generate valid integrity information for each TL-UL response it produces. The integrity must cover the response fields as required by the configured integrity scheme.

### 8.3 Data Integrity Generation

When data integrity generation is enabled, the adapter must generate integrity information for the data returned on a TL-UL read response. This mode assumes the SRAM itself does not store integrity bits; therefore, the SRAM data width does not need to be extended for integrity in this mode.

### 8.4 Data Integrity Pass-through

When data integrity pass-through is enabled, the adapter must not generate data integrity itself. Instead, it must transfer integrity bits unchanged:

- On writes, the integrity bits associated with the incoming TL-UL write data must be forwarded to the SRAM along with the data. The SRAM write mask must enable the integrity bits for the accessed word so that they are written.
- On reads, the integrity bits read from the SRAM must be forwarded unchanged as part of the TL-UL read response.

In pass-through mode, the SRAM data path is wider by the integrity width. To preserve the stored integrity, the adapter must not mask out read data bytes in this mode. The complete data word, including integrity bits, must be returned for the selected TL-UL word slice.

## 9. Reset and Output State

At reset, all TL-UL response outputs, SRAM request outputs, write-enable, address, write-data, and write-mask outputs must be brought to defined, inactive values. After reset is released, the adapter must be ready to receive TL-UL requests.

All outputs must remain valid and must not enter an unknown state during normal operation.

## 10. Summary of Behavioral Requirements

- Translate each TL-UL read or write request into one SRAM access.
- Accept requests only when they can be tracked and, for normal requests, only when the SRAM side grants the access.
- Never send an erroring request to the SRAM; return an error response instead.
- Return write acknowledgements without waiting for SRAM write completion.
- Return read responses only when SRAM read data is available.
- Preserve request order and return responses in order.
- Support partial-word accesses when configured, and reject them when disabled.
- Support wide SRAM words by mapping addresses and byte enables appropriately.
- Support configurable integrity checking, generation, and pass-through.
- Report command integrity failures with a sticky output in addition to the per-transaction error response.
